text:
Lakers to host Warriors in 2026-27 NBA season opener on Oct. 21
The Los Angeles Lakers will host the Golden State Warriors on Oct. 21 as part of the NBA’s Opening Week primetime slate, according to an Aug. 11 announcement. This marks the first time since the 2018-19 season that the Lakers will not be featured on Opening Night.
The two teams have taken different approaches during the offseason before their scheduled matchup. The Lakers have restructured their roster around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, moving on from six key contributors from last season. In contrast, the Warriors are returning with nearly all of last year’s players.
Doncic and the Lakers will begin their season at home against Stephen Curry and the Warriors at 7:00 p.m. PT in a game broadcast as part of an ESPN doubleheader. The earlier game features Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball with the Minnesota Timberwolves facing Giannis Antetokounmpo, who is making his debut for the Miami Heat.
The absence of Los Angeles from Opening Night comes after eight consecutive seasons, due to a high-profile Western Conference opener between the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs, whose rivalry intensified following a seven-game Western Conference Finals series won by San Antonio last year.
Elsewhere in Opening Week, LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers are set to play against reigning champions New York Knicks during banner night at Madison Square Garden.
